title: Financial pressure is construct-dependent and should be treated as separate planning signals
headline: Financial pressure increased while social reconnection also increased in Australia between 2020 and 2025.
interpretation: The independent U.S. series do not move identically: both SHED adult measures are flat from 2022 to 2024, USDA household food insecurity rises slightly, and JPMorganChase reports a higher household cash-liquidity endpoint when disposable income and short-term credit are included. Together they show construct-dependent, non-uniform resource pressure, not a common trend estimate.
counter_signal: Social contact increased alongside the financial-pressure measures; the evidence does not support a simple collapse-of-participation story.

uncertainty.shed: The public chart artifact supplies point estimates only; the 2024 codebook identifies 12,295 respondents, but no interval was attached to either normalized SHED series.
uncertainty.usda: USDA publishes statistical-significance guidance and calculates standard errors with balanced repeated replication; the 2022-2024 national points are not statistically distinguishable on the published comparison.
uncertainty.use: Keep the comparison descriptive and unpooled until year-specific intervals or a reproducible variance extract is attached to both series.

decision_use: Use this card to frame scenario questions about household and consumer pressure. Do not pool unlike denominators, infer causality, or label a company population from the external series.
company_gate: No internal bridge until a compatible independent outcome, source-specific rights approval, a named decision contract, and privacy/access review pass.
next_action: Attach year-specific uncertainty or a reproducible variance extract, complete artifact-level rights review, and keep the lane as mechanism context until the qualification gates pass.
boundary: This is a reader-facing external evidence card, not a qualified trend, causal result, forecast, market estimate, legal clearance, or company finding.
